question: Why does bio_all diverge at toy scale on real text, and what AdamW LR should GPTSynaptic's 1-D block parameters take?
finding: GPTSynaptic.setup_optimizers gave every 1-D block parameter (LayerNorm gains/biases, linear biases, PostsynapticHebb.fast/slow multiplicative gains) the embedding LR 0.2*(d/768)^-0.5 = 0.49 at d=128. bio_all goes NaN within 20 steps; a separate scalar LR of 0.01 trains stably and also improves synaptic_off.

protocol.arms: vanilla (--synapses=0); synaptic_off (the matrix anchor's --syn_cfg overrides); bio_all (default SynapticConfig); --scalar_lr in {0.003, 0.01, 0.04} vs the legacy 0.49
protocol.data: WikiText-2 raw (pytorch/examples word_language_model data) as parquet: train split -> shard 0, valid+test -> shard 1 (held-out val). FineWeb-Edu was unreachable from this host (huggingface.co denied by egress policy). 4,096-token rustbpe tokenizer trained on shard 0.
protocol.hardware: cpu:x86_64, 4 cores, two runs concurrently at OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 (tok/s not comparable across arms)
protocol.selection: single seed; the value was chosen on the held-out val bpb, so this is a recipe choice, not a measured bio effect

measurement_regime.seed_axis: init_seed reseeds weights and the presyn RNG (636e955)

bio_all_legacy_lr.note: stopped after the loss went NaN at step 12

no_claim: One seed at 2 layers x 128 dims on WikiText-2: says nothing about whether biology helps; it says the synaptic optimizer recipe no longer diverges.
